summary: OgleMark: session-coordinator failover amplification causing retries, duplicate acknowledgements, and elevated 5xx rate — after-action
description:
Issue summary:
During a sustained traffic burst from OgleMark (enterprise tenant with heavy streaming usage) the session-coordinator entered a failover amplification loop. The coordinator retried session handoffs aggressively while downstream autoscaler and serving pools were already saturated. Symptoms included elevated 5xx rate (peaked at ~18% for the tenant), duplicate acknowledgement messages seen by the customer (duplicate completions for the same prompt), and streaming connections that briefly stalled then reconnected, producing overlapping responses.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: duplicate completions for chat sessions, delayed first-byte for streaming responses, occasional client disconnects.
- Business: SLA exposure for OgleMark (enterprise), customer escalation to account team, preliminary billing discrepancy for retried tokens.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-18 02:13 UTC: sudden traffic spike from OgleMark (large campaign).
- 02:15 UTC: session-coordinator observed increased handoff rate; autoscaler began scaling but lagged due to GPU provisioning delay.
- 02:18-02:32 UTC: retries amplified; duplicate ack events observed in logs. 5xx rate for the tenant peaked at ~18%; global p99 tail latency rose from 300ms baseline to 2.4s on affected routes.
- 02:35 UTC: Support engaged SRE; temporary mitigation applied (throttle window + session-affinity enforcement).
- 03:02 UTC: mitigation rolled out; duplicate completions dropped to baseline; customer connections stabilized.

Environment:
- prod cluster us-east-1; dedicated placement group for enterprise tenants; kernel selection: quantized-ff16.

Steps to reproduce (dev-repro guidance):
1) Simulate OgleMark traffic pattern: burst of ~2.5k concurrent streaming sessions over 2 minutes with frequent reconnects and several long-running completions (>2k tokens).
2) Force KV cache flush between handoffs to simulate coordination mismatch.
3) Observe session-coordinator logs for repeated handoff attempts and note overlapping ACK messages to client websocket.

Logs / traces / dashboards:
- Kibana session-coordinator logs: https://kibana.internal/redwood/session-coord/_search?q=oglemark+2026-02-18
- Grafana: tenant OgleMark dashboard (5xx rate, tail latency): https://grafana.internal/d/oglemark/tenant-health
- Jaeger trace sample: https://jaeger.internal/trace/0a1b2c3d

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Throttle backlog for session handoffs to 30 reqs/s for the tenant for 20 minutes.
- Forced session-affinity header enforcement to avoid cross-pool handoffs while autoscaler completed scale-up.
- Issued a one-time billing credit hold for retried tokens pending audit.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
- Session-coordinator aggressively retried in-flight handoffs when it received partial ACK timeouts, without respecting downstream autoscaler backpressure signals. The combination of aggressive retries plus a temporary delay in GPU pod readiness led to a classic amplification (retries -> more load -> more retries). Additionally, KV cache invalidations during the spike caused duplicate session state writes, which the client observed as duplicate acknowledgements/completions.

Permanent fixes / recommended changes (short list):
- Add a coordinated backoff layer: session-coordinator must respect serving-runtime backpressure and circuit-breaker states before retrying handoffs.
- Ensure KV cache write idempotency: include session-version tokens to avoid duplicate ACKs on replays.
- Autoscaler tuning: reduce minimum pod init latency by pre-warming GPU pool for known enterprise tenants during campaign windows.
- Post-incident: run a chaos test that simulates KV flush + heavy reconnects to validate the fix.

Customer communication (summary sent to account team):
We acknowledged the customer within 10 minutes. We implemented a throttle-and-affinity mitigation and returned to normal within ~47 minutes. Engineering root cause analysis is in progress; we committed to a mitigation plan and a timeline for a permanent fix. Billing team flagged retried tokens for credit review.
investigation_notes:
- SRE note: coordinator metrics showed handoff retry rate increased 12x relative to baseline.
- Trace analysis: several traces show the coordinator re-emitting ACK messages on state refresh; duplicates had identical session_id but different sequence numbers.
- Hypothesis validated in staging repro: when KV flush and pod provisioning delay are combined, the coordinator path produces duplicate writes.
- Cross-team sync: scheduler and autoscaler confirmed a 90s median pod readiness increase correlating with the window.
- Security check: no indication of malicious clients or unauthorized replays.

Links referenced during investigation:
- Slack thread: #support-oglemark (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C08XYZ)
- Runbook: Session Coordinator Circuit Breaker (https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/OPS/Session+Coordinator+Circuit+Breaker)
resolution:
- Deployed a hotfix to session-coordinator that adds progressive retry backoff and checks autoscaler circuit state before retrying handoffs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/session-coordinator/pull/614).
- Added session-version token to KV writes to make them idempotent; duplicate ACKs no longer issued.
- Adjusted autoscaler prewarm policy for enterprise tenants to reduce pod readiness latency during known campaign windows.
- Issued a provisional billing credit to OgleMark while finance audits token retention logs.
- Customer notified and account team assigned follow-up call to review SLA credit and timeline for full rollout (Marcus Lee to lead).
